intro_html: A Beef Manhattan is a Midwest diner plate: shredded roast beef and brown gravy spooned over mashed potatoes, no ceremony, no garnish. It shows up on lunch counters from Indiana to Nebraska and it has kept people fed cheaply for seventy years. We build it in a slow cooker and portion it into bowls. Each bowl carries 48 grams of protein and 581 calories for about $4.49.
cost_closing_html: About $4.49 a bowl. Six ingredients, one of them potatoes, and the gravy comes out of two packets that cost less than a cup of coffee.
shop_smart: Brown gravy mix and onion soup mix both come in multi packet boxes. The per packet price is lower and they sit in the pantry for a year without complaint.
Russet potatoes mash better than waxy ones and cost less per pound. Buy the big bag and use the extras for the other potato recipes in this section.
Chuck roast is what a Manhattan is supposed to be made of. This is one of the rare cases where the cheap answer is also the traditional one.
Red wine vinegar is a long life pantry bottle. A little goes in here to cut the salt from the two seasoning packets, so do not skip it.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the chuck roast dry, season it with salt and black pepper, and sear it in the olive oil until it is browned on every side.
Set the roast in the slow cooker and sprinkle the brown gravy mix and onion soup mix over the top.
Add the red wine vinegar and enough water to come about a third of the way up the roast.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the beef shreds with no effort.
About 40 minutes before you portion, peel and boil the potatoes until a knife slides through, then drain and mash them with some of the hot gravy from the cooker.
Shred the beef in the cooker and stir it through the gravy so nothing dries out.
Taste the gravy. Two seasoning packets bring plenty of salt, so it likely needs pepper rather than more salt.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Spread that weight of mashed potatoes into each container first, then spoon an even weight of shredded beef and gravy over the top. Each bowl lands at 581 calories with 48 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Diner style beef and gravy for about $4.49 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Beef Manhattan bowls meal prep: slow cooked shredded chuck roast in brown gravy spooned over mashed potatoes, Midwest diner style. 581 calories, 48g protein, about $4.49 per serving.
head.keywords: beef manhattan, open faced roast beef, shredded beef and gravy, mashed potato bowls, budget meal prep, midwest diner recipes
steps: Sear the seasoned chuck roast in olive oil until browned all over.
Set it in the slow cooker with brown gravy mix, onion soup mix, vinegar, and water.
Cook on low 8 hours until the beef shreds easily.
Boil and mash the potatoes with some of the hot gravy.
Shred the beef into the gravy and portion over the potatoes into 14 containers.
